newsitem.title: ITALY: U.S. troops leave for possible Zaire evacuation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. troops leave for possible Zaire evacuation.

text.p: The first contingent of U.S. solidiers left Italy for Africa on Sunday to prepare for a possible American evacuation from Zaire.
The 27 servicemen, primarily from the Southern European Task Force based in Vicenza, Italy, left from an air force base in Aviano, air force Major Bryan Holt said.
He said more troops would be leaving from Aviano, north of Vicenza, throughout the day. Most were headed for Brazzaville, Congo.
Among those who left on Sunday was army Major General Edwin Smith, commander of the Southern European Task force and commander of the joint task force for Operation Guardian Retrieval.

On Friday the U.S. Department of Defence directed the U.S. European Command to deploy forces, consisting of several hundred personnel, as part of contingency planning for a possible future evacuation from Zaire.
The U.S. forces will join French troops and planes already in nearby Gabon and Congo in case evacuations from strife-torn Zaire become necessary. Belgium is also sending troops.
Zaire's long-time ruler President Mobutu Sese Seko, 66, is ill with cancer and rebels led by Laurent Kabila have seized about a fifth of the sprawling central African country.
